children: Bahri, a global leader in transportation and logistics, and International Maritime Industries (IMI), the largest integrated maritime facility in the Mena region, have signed a contract for the construction of three Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) at IMI’s facility in Saudi Arabia, in conjunction with the Saudi Maritime & Logistics Congress.
As per the contract, valued at SAR1.7 billion, IMI will build three VLCCs, each with a capacity of 320,000 deadweight tonnes (DWT).
These vessels will be equipped with advanced energy-efficiency technologies and are scheduled for phased delivery between 2029 and 2030.
The contract forms part of Bahri’s strategy to modernise its fleet and expand its operational capabilities to meet the evolving demands of global energy markets.
With this deal, the total number of vessels Bahri has contracted to be built in Saudi Arabia since the beginning of the year has risen to nine, comprising six Ultramax bulk carriers and three VLCCs.

On the agreement, Bahri CEO Eng. Ahmed Alsubaey said: "Fleet modernisation is a key pillar of our long-term strategy. This contract enables us to strengthen our capabilities with modern, more efficient vessels, while expanding our collaboration with IMI and supporting the development of Saudi Arabia’s maritime supply chain."
International Maritime Industries CEO Eng. Abdullah Al-Ghamdi said this milestone reflects the continued advancement of Saudi Arabia’s maritime industry.
"We look forward to supporting Bahri’s future requirements and contributing to the localization of shipbuilding capabilities in line with the Kingdom’s Vision objectives," he added.-
